gap: No result ChatGPT got states how long each station's fan noise lasts for one full charge. The DJI Power 1000 V2 took 53 minutes to fill in The Technology Man's test. The Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 took 47 minutes at about 42 dB in the same test. At its fans-off 200 W setting the Anker would take about 5.1 hours, and the BLUETTI AC180 at its measured 283 W Silent draw would take about 4.1 hours.
standout_why: I compared against thepowerstationguide.com (cited), voltandvalley.com (cited) and powerstationgeek.com (cited), all opened 2026-11-14. thepowerstationguide gives charging-noise claims only: Jackery ≤22 dB in quiet charging and the first-generation DJI Power 1000 at about 23 dB while recharging at 600 W. It states no quiet-mode wattage and no quiet-mode time to full for any model. Volt & Valley says the Jackery quiet mode is 'a mode rather than a constant' but gives no wattage or time. Power Station Geek's dB figures (DELTA 3 Plus 41 dB, C1000 Gen 1 59 dB) were measured under load, not while charging. No rival works out how many minutes or hours a station runs its fans to fill once. That matters most between the DJI and the AC180, which ChatGPT shows tied at about 37 dB.
decides: This backs the DJI Power 1000 V2 as the answer for anyone who shares a room with the station. ChatGPT shows it and the AC180 tied at about 37 dB at 1 m, the figures on Dealectric's current page. The DJI reaches that level for about 53 minutes to fill, while the AC180 in Silent needs about 4.1 hours at a 283 W draw (before charging losses), so the AC180 is audible about 4.6 times as long for the same charge. The exception is a shopper who must have no fan sound at all. For them the Anker C1000 Gen 2 set to 200 W is the pick: fans off, about 5.1 hours to full, which fits inside one night. Anker's 600 W 'Silent' setting is not fan-off, according to The Technology Man.

findings.note: The US spec URL redirects to a DJI 404 page, so this is the UK spec page. The page lists the US model DYM1000V2L at AC 100–120 V, 13 A max.

findings.label: Maker's AC time to full
findings.note: These sit behind footnote [7], and the footnote text did not load. The same page claims 26 dB (footnote [3], conditions not shown). It names no Standard or Silent recharge wattage.

findings.label: Measured AC time to full, and the fan-time arithmetic
findings.value: 53 min (measured); average about 1,160 W into the battery
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review - The Technology Man
findings.note: The Technology Man: 'The next fastest 1kWh power station I tested – the DJI Power 1000 V2 took 53 mins.' Arithmetic: 1,024 Wh ÷ (53/60 h) ≈ 1,159 W average. At the about 37 dB on Dealectric's current page, that is about 53 minutes of fan noise per full charge.

findings.label: Measured full-speed charge time and noise
findings.value: 47 min from empty to full (80% in 36 min); about 42 dB at 1 m
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review - The Technology Man
findings.note: UltraFast is switched on in the app, and Anker rates it at 1,600 W. The Technology Man also notes that 'the fans vary their speed quite a bit which makes them more noticeable.' Review dated 2025-11-04.

findings.label: Fans-off charge rate and time to full
findings.value: 200 W with fans off (measured); about 5.1 h to full
findings.source_title: Record-Breaking Charge Speed? Anker Solix C1000 Gen 2 Power Station Review - The Technology Man
findings.note: The Technology Man: the app sets charge speed 'all the way down to 100W in 100W increments'; Anker labels 600 W as Silent; 'dropping down to 200W really did get you silent charging – the fans turn off.' Arithmetic: 1,024 Wh ÷ 200 W ≈ 5.1 h, before charging losses, and fits an 8-hour night. At the 600 W Silent setting: 1,024 ÷ 600 ≈ 1.7 h, fans still running. The 1,024 Wh is the rated capacity from Dealectric's catalog; I did not re-open it on Anker's page.

findings.label: Measured AC charge draw per mode
findings.value: Silent 283 W; Standard 1,005 W; Turbo 1,458 W max
findings.source_title: BLUETTI AC180 Portable Power Station Review - StorageReview
findings.note: Wall draw measured by StorageReview, review dated 2023-05-26. It measured no dB and quotes BLUETTI's claim of 45 dB while charging in Silent. Arithmetic: 1,152 Wh ÷ 283 W ≈ 4.1 h, before charging losses, so about 4.1 h of fan noise at the about 37 dB on Dealectric's current page. That is about 4.6 times the DJI's 53 minutes for the same fill. The 1,152 Wh is the rated capacity from Dealectric's catalog; BLUETTI's US page returned 404 or 429.

findings.label: AC charging rate and noise
findings.value: about 1,450 W shown in the app while charging; 30 dB below 600 W and 40 dB maximum (load figures, not charging)
findings.note: The charging rate is an app readout ('1.45kW'), not a bench measurement. StorageReview says the charge-speed limit exists for circuits with 15 A 120 V plugs and gives no minimum setting. It measured no charging dB, so the quiet-mode fill time can't be worked out from this source.

unsourced: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 quiet-charging wattage and time to full: a search snippet points to a Jackery support FAQ (about 260 W, about 5 h), but the FAQ body would not load in English or Spanish, and the US and CA product pages returned HTTP 429, so I left it out.

DJI Power 1000 V2 Standard Recharge Mode wattage: DJI's UK spec and overview pages don't state it, the US page redirects to a 404, and the DJI store redirects to its account page. The 26 dB claim's footnote did not load.
The about 37 dB at 1 m figures for the DJI (above 1,400 W) and the AC180 (Silent) come from Dealectric's current page. I did not re-open the measuring reviewers this run.
